name: orb_15min_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: The first 15 minutes of the session concentrates institutional order flow from overnight decisions, creating a defined range. Breakout from this range signals directional commitment. The inefficiency exists because retail traders are slow to react to the directional signal embedded in institutional flow, and many systematic players wait for 30-min or 1-hour confirmations. Not fully arbitraged because the signal is noisy — win rate is moderate — and sizing constraints limit capacity for larger funds.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 constituents with ADV > ₹100cr and ATR(20) > 1.5%

indicators.name: orb_width
indicators.purpose: range width as % — skip if too wide

long.confirmation: close above orb_high on the breakout bar (not just wick)

short.confirmation: close below orb_low on the breakout bar

exit.stop_loss: opposite side of ORB (orb_low for longs, orb_high for shorts)
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after 1x orb_width profit
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters ORB and closes inside for 3 consecutive bars

filters.volume_filter: breakout bar volume must be > 1.5x 20-bar avg
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when nifty50_return_15min > 0, shorts when < 0
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy, monthly expiry

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, but crowding is increasing

weaknesses: False breakouts are frequent — estimated 55-60% of breakouts reverse within 30 bars. Volume confirmation helps but doesn't eliminate the problem.
Gap days with extreme opening ranges (>1.5% width) create poor risk/reward. The stop at the opposite ORB boundary becomes too wide.
Crowded strategy — ORB is one of the most backtested retail strategies in India. Alpha decay is real. The edge is in the filters, not the base concept.
prior_art: Classic Opening Range Breakout (Toby Crabel). Widely known. Specific value is in the width filter and volume confirmation.
notes: Consider A/B testing 15-min vs 30-min opening range. 30-min may have fewer false breakouts but worse risk/reward.
